newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Blast at Damascus bus station, 15 said killed.
newsitem.headline: Blast at Damascus bus station, 15 said killed.

text.p: An explosion hit a bus station in the Syrian capital Damascus on Tuesday, a resident diplomat said on Thursday, while a recently returned traveller reported that 15 people had been killed by a bomb.

The diplomat said large numbers of police sealed off the area after the explosion in the Baramkeh district and streets were blocked with traffic trying to evacuate the area. He said the blast was said to have occurred at 1.30 p.m. on Tuesday and apparently destroyed a small bus.

The diplomat, speaking by telephone, stressed that reliable information was very difficult to obtain and that on Thursday there was no sign of any incident at the bus station which lies close to the international fair and museum and serves the route to Lebanon.
A traveller who was in Damascus on Tuesday said the blast was caused by a bomb.

"A bomb placed in a bag exploded in the luggage compartment of a bus at Al-Intilak Centre, the main taxi and bus stop in Damascus. The bus belonged to Trans Tours company and was heading to Aleppo (in northern Syria)," the traveller said.
"At least 15 people were killed and 50 wounded in the blast."

It was not known who caused the blast. Reports of such incidents are rare in Syria where the media is strictly controlled. Some incidents earlier in 1996 were attributed to elements in Turkey. Last month there were also one or two attacks on Syrian targets in neighbouring Lebanon.
Leaflets distributed in Beirut last month condemned Syria's military presence in Lebanon and criticised Lebanon's pro-Syrian government.
Syrian government officials contacted in Damascus had no immediate comment on the reported explosion.
